title: InfoQ Opens Enrollment for New AI-Assisted Engineering Online Certification Program
gist: InfoQ launched a paid, five-week AI-Assisted Engineering certification aimed at senior engineers running coding agents on production codebases, built around the idea that teams are adopting agents faster than they build the verification 'harness' — permissions, review gates, and CI checks — around them.

insights.claim: The InfoQ AI-Assisted Engineering certification explicitly targets senior engineers and architects already running coding agents on production codebases with years of history, not toy demo apps, teaching what an agent is allowed to do, how to catch it when wrong, and how to prove to an organization that agent-generated code is valid, scalable, and maintainable.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Indicates real market demand for structured verification practices around coding agents in enterprise settings, not just greenfield experimentation.
insights.locator: This certification is for senior engineers and architects

insights.claim: Program co-facilitator Zichuan Xiong (Head of AIOps at Thoughtworks) frames the core problem as teams adopting coding agents faster than they build verification around them, defining the 'harness' as everything outside the model — permissions, sensors, review gates, and CI checks that let an agent self-correct before a human sees the change.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Articulates a concrete framing (the 'harness' gap) relevant to anyone building or evaluating AI code-review, permissioning, or CI-verification tooling as a product category.
insights.quote: Teams are adopting coding agents faster than they're building the verification around them. The harness is everything outside the model: permissions, sensors, review gates, and CI checks that let an agent correct itself before a human ever sees the change.

insights.claim: The five-week curriculum moves through a specific sequence — least-privilege agent onboarding and sandboxing, converting vague issue tickets into verifiable requirements, separating code generation from review via an independent harness rather than letting the generating agent grade its own work, pushing verification into CI with governance for unattended runs, and finally codifying review findings into reusable rules — outlining an emerging canonical workflow for operating coding agents safely at scale.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: A benchmarkable workflow (generation/review separation, CI-embedded verification, rule codification) that engineering leaders can compare their own agent-adoption practices against.

insights.claim: InfoQ is running the AI-Assisted Engineering certification alongside four other paid five-week cohort programs — AI Security & Privacy Engineering (Katharine Jarmul), Architecture (Luca Mezzalira), and Engineering Leadership (Michelle Brush) — each priced at $1,470, suggesting a scaling paid-education business layered on top of its conference and publishing operations.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: A revenue-diversification signal for InfoQ/QCon's parent business into recurring paid certification, worth tracking alongside its conference and content revenue lines.

insights.claim: Live sessions in the program are deliberately not recorded so that participants can openly discuss their own organizations' permissions models, review gates, and failures, with the cohort and facilitators continuing the discussion in a private Slack channel between sessions.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Design choice aimed at extracting real proprietary practices from participants, which also implies the program's value lies partly in peer benchmarking, not just instructional content.
